Karnataka.fact: The expansion of the Hoysala Empire brought minor parts of modern Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu under its rule.  In the early 14th century, Harihara and Bukka Raya established the Vijayanagara empire with its capital, Hosapattana (later named Vijayanagara), on the banks of the Tungabhadra River in the modern Bellary district.  Under the rule of Krishnadevaraya, a distinct form of literature and architecture evolved.  The empire rose as a bulwark against Muslim advances into South India, which it completely controlled for over two centuries.  In 1537, Kempe Gowda I, a chieftain of the Vijayanagara Empire, widely held as the founder of modern Bengaluru, built a fort and established the area around it as Bengaluru Pete.  In 1565, Karnataka and the rest of South India experienced a major geopolitical shift when the Vijayanagara empire fell to a confederation of Islamic sultanates in the Battle of Talikota.  The Bijapur Sultanate, which had risen after the demise of the Bahmani Sultanate of Bidar, soon took control of much of the Deccan; it was defeated by the Mughals in the late 17th century

In the period that followed, parts of northern Karnataka were ruled by the Nizam of Hyderabad, the Maratha Empire, the British, and other powers.  In the south, the Mysore Kingdom, a former vassal of the Vijayanagara Empire, was briefly independent.  With the death of Krishnaraja Wodeyar II, Haidar Ali, the commander-in-chief of the Mysore army, gained control of the region.  After his death, the kingdom was inherited by his son Tipu Sultan.  To contain European expansion in South India, Hyder Ali and later Tipu Sultan fought four significant Anglo-Mysore Wars, the last of which resulted in Tippu Sultan's death and the incorporation of Mysore into British India in 1799.  Mysore was restored to the Wodeyars, and the Kingdom of Mysore became a princely state outside but in a subsidiary alliance with British India

Kartikeya.question: He is generally described as the son of the deities Shiva and _____ and the brother of Ganesha
Kartikeya.fact: He is generally described as the son of the deities Shiva and Parvati and the brother of Ganesha.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Apart from significant _____ worship and temples in South India, he is worshipped as Mahasena and Kumara in North and East India
Kartikeya.fact: Kaumaram is the Hindu denomination that primarily venerates Kartikeya. Apart from significant Kaumaram worship and temples in South India, he is worshipped as Mahasena and Kumara in North and East India.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Muruga is a tutelary deity mentioned in _____ literature, of the Kurinji region
Kartikeya.fact: Muruga is a tutelary deity mentioned in Tamil Sangam literature, of the Kurinji region.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: He is considered as the patron deity of Tamil language and literary works such as _____āṟṟuppaṭai by Nakkīraṉãr and Tiruppukal by Arunagirinathar are devoted to Muruga
Kartikeya.fact: He is considered as the patron deity of Tamil language and literary works such as Tirumurukāṟṟuppaṭai by Nakkīraṉãr and Tiruppukal by Arunagirinathar are devoted to Muruga.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: He is typically represented as an ever-youthful man, riding or near an Indian peafowl (named _____), and sometimes with an emblem of a rooster on his banner
Kartikeya.fact: He is typically represented as an ever-youthful man, riding or near an Indian peafowl (named Paravani), and sometimes with an emblem of a rooster on his banner.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: He wields a spear called the vel, supposedly given to him by his mother _____
Kartikeya.fact: He wields a spear called the vel, supposedly given to him by his mother Parvati.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: He is described to have aged quickly from childhood, becoming a warrior, leading the army of the devas and credited with destroying asuras including _____ and Surapadma
Kartikeya.fact: He is described to have aged quickly from childhood, becoming a warrior, leading the army of the devas and credited with destroying asuras including Tarakasura and Surapadma.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: He is regarded as a philosopher who taught the pursuit of an ethical life and the theology of _____
Kartikeya.fact: He is regarded as a philosopher who taught the pursuit of an ethical life and the theology of Shaiva Siddhanta.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: According to the _____, six divine sparks emerged from Shiva, forming six separate baby boys
Kartikeya.fact: According to the Skanda Purana, six divine sparks emerged from Shiva, forming six separate baby boys.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: These boys were raised by handmaidens known as the _____
Kartikeya.fact: These boys were raised by handmaidens called the Krittikas. Kartikeya means "of the Krittikas" in Sanskrit.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: According to _____ literature, he is known by 108 different names, though other names also exist in common usage
Kartikeya.fact: According to Hindu literature, he is known by 108 different names, though other names also exist in common usage.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: On ancient coins featuring his images, his name appears inscribed as Kumara, _____, or Brahmanyadeva
Kartikeya.fact: Most common amongst these include Skanda (from skanda-, 'to leap or to attack'), Muruga ('handsome'), Kumara ('youthful'), Subrahmanya ('transparent'), Senthil ('victorious'), Vēlaṇ ('wielder of vel'), Swaminatha ('ruler of gods'), Saravaṇabhava ('born amongst the reeds'), Arumukha or Shanmukha ('six faced'), Dhandapani ('wielder of mace') and Kandha ('cloud'). On ancient coins featuring his images, his name appears inscribed as Kumara, Brahmanya, or Brahmanyadeva.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: On some ancient Indo-_____ coins, his name appears in Greek script as Skanda, Kumara, and Vishaka
Kartikeya.fact: On some ancient Indo-Scythian coins, his name appears in Greek script as Skanda, Kumara, and Vishaka.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: According to _____, asura Tarakasura performed tapas to propitiate the creator god Brahma
Kartikeya.fact: According to Shiva Purana, asura Tarakasura performed tapas to propitiate the creator god Brahma.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Brahma granted him two boons: one, that none shall be his equal in all of the three worlds, and two, that only a son of _____ could slay him
Kartikeya.fact: The Shalya Parva and the Anushasana Parva of the third-century BCE Hindu epic Mahabharata narrate the legend of Skanda, presenting him as the son of Maheshvara (Shiva) and Parvati: Shiva and Parvati were disturbed during sex, causing Shiva to inadvertently spill his semen. According to Shiva Purana, asura Tarakasura performed tapas to propitiate the creator god Brahma.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: As Shiva was a yogi and thus unlikely to bear children, _____ was armed with near immortality
Kartikeya.fact: According to Shiva Purana, asura Tarakasura performed tapas to propitiate the creator god Brahma. As Shiva was a yogi and thus unlikely to bear children, Tarakasura was armed with near immortality.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: In his quest to rule the three worlds, he expelled the devas from _____
Kartikeya.fact: In his quest to rule the three worlds, he expelled the devas from Svarga.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Indra, the king of devas, devised a scheme to disrupt Shiva's meditation and beguile him with thoughts of love, so that he could sire an offspring and thusly end _____'s immortality
Kartikeya.fact: As Shiva was a yogi and thus unlikely to bear children, Tarakasura was armed with near immortality. Indra, the king of devas, devised a scheme to disrupt Shiva's meditation and beguile him with thoughts of love, so that he could sire an offspring and thusly end Tarakasura's immortality.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Shiva was engaged in meditation, and hardly noticed the courtship of _____, the daughter of Himavan who sought him as her consort
Kartikeya.fact: Shiva was engaged in meditation, and hardly noticed the courtship of Parvati, the daughter of Himavan who sought him as her consort. But Shiva's attention then turned towards Parvati, who had performed tapas in order to win his affection, and married her, then conceiving Kartikeya.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Indra tasked god of love _____ and his consort Rati to disturb Shiva
Kartikeya.fact: Indra tasked god of love Kamadeva and his consort Rati to disturb Shiva. Shiva was furious with the act and burnt Kamadeva to ashes.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Shiva was furious with the act and burnt _____ to ashes
Kartikeya.fact: Indra tasked god of love Kamadeva and his consort Rati to disturb Shiva. Shiva was furious with the act and burnt Kamadeva to ashes.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: When the devas pleaded to _____ for his assistance, he manifested five additional heads on his body, and a divine spark emerged from each of them
Kartikeya.fact: But Shiva's attention then turned towards Parvati, who had performed tapas in order to win his affection, and married her, then conceiving Kartikeya. According to the seventeenth-century CE text Kanda Puranam (the Tamil rendition of the older Skanda Purana), the asura brothers Surapadma, Simhamukha and Tarakasura performed tapas to Shiva, who granted them with various weapons and a wish wherein they could only be killed by the son of Shiva, which offered them near-immortality.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Initially, the wind god _____ carried the sparks, later handing them to the fire god Agni because of the unbearable heat
Kartikeya.fact: Initially, the wind god Vayu carried the sparks, later handing them to the fire god Agni because of the unbearable heat.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Agni deposited the sparks in the _____ river
Kartikeya.fact: Agni deposited the sparks in the Ganges river. The water in the Ganges began to evaporate due to the intense heat of the sparks.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: The water in the _____ began to evaporate due to the intense heat of the sparks
Kartikeya.fact: Agni deposited the sparks in the Ganges river. The water in the Ganges began to evaporate due to the intense heat of the sparks.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Ganga took them to _____ lake, where the sparks developed into six baby boys
Kartikeya.fact: Ganga took them to Saravana lake, where the sparks developed into six baby boys.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: The six boys were then raised by the _____ and they were later fused into one by Parvati
Kartikeya.fact: The six boys were then raised by the Krittikas and they were later fused into one by Parvati. When the Krittikas bathe in the river, they are impregnated and give birth to Kartikeya.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: 'Birth of _____') from the fifth-century CE narrates a similar story on his birth wherein Agni carries the semen of Shiva and deposits them in Bhagirathi River (headstream of Ganges)
Kartikeya.fact: 'Birth of Kumara') from the fifth-century CE narrates a similar story on his birth wherein Agni carries the semen of Shiva and deposits them in Bhagirathi River (headstream of Ganges).

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: It is narrated that Agni goes to meet the wives of the _____ (seven great sages) and, while none of the wives reciprocates Agni's feelings of love, Svaha is present and attracted to Agni
Kartikeya.fact: It is narrated that Agni goes to meet the wives of the Saptarshi (seven great sages) and, while none of the wives reciprocates Agni's feelings of love, Svaha is present and attracted to Agni.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Svaha takes the form of six of the wives, one by one, and has sex with _____ six times
Kartikeya.fact: An alternate account of Kartikeya's parentage is narrated in the Vana Parva of the Mahabharata, where he is described as the son of Agni and Svaha. It is narrated that Agni goes to meet the wives of the Saptarshi (seven great sages) and, while none of the wives reciprocates Agni's feelings of love, Svaha is present and attracted to Agni.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: She is unable to take the form of _____, Vasishtha's wife, because of Arundhati's extraordinary virtuous powers
Kartikeya.fact: She is unable to take the form of Arundhati, Vasishtha's wife, because of Arundhati's extraordinary virtuous powers.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Svaha deposits the semen of Agni into the reeds of _____ river, where it develops and is born as the six-headed Skanda
Kartikeya.fact: Svaha deposits the semen of Agni into the reeds of Ganges river, where it develops and is born as the six-headed Skanda. In his childhood, he fiddles with the orbits of planets, stacks the mountains in Kailasha on top of Mount Meru and stops the flow of River Ganges, among other feats.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: In his childhood, he fiddles with the orbits of planets, stacks the mountains in Kailasha on top of _____ and stops the flow of River Ganges, among other feats
Kartikeya.fact: In his childhood, he fiddles with the orbits of planets, stacks the mountains in Kailasha on top of Mount Meru and stops the flow of River Ganges, among other feats.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: He imprisons _____ as he could not explain the meaning of Aum
Kartikeya.fact: He imprisons Brahma as he could not explain the meaning of Aum.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: According to the _____, the devas and gods gift him various objects and animals
Kartikeya.fact: According to the Mahabharata, the devas and gods gift him various objects and animals.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: As per _____, sage Narada once visited Shiva at Kailasha and presented him with a Gnana palam (fruit of knowledge)
Kartikeya.fact: As per Kanda Puranam, sage Narada once visited Shiva at Kailasha and presented him with a Gnana palam (fruit of knowledge).

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: However, _____ surmised that the world was no more than his parents Shiva and Shakti combined, circumambulated them, and won the fruit
Kartikeya.fact: Shiva expressed his intention of dividing the fruit between his two sons, Ganesha and Kartikeya, but Narada counseled that the fruit could not be divided. However, Ganesha surmised that the world was no more than his parents Shiva and Shakti combined, circumambulated them, and won the fruit.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: He discarded all his material belongings and left _____ to take up abode in the Palani Hills as a hermit
Kartikeya.fact: He discarded all his material belongings and left Kailasha to take up abode in the Palani Hills as a hermit.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Shiva granted him celestial weapons and the divine spear vel, an embodiment of the power of Shakti (_____)
Kartikeya.fact: Shiva granted him celestial weapons and the divine spear vel, an embodiment of the power of Shakti (Parvati).

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: These nine men were borne by nine lesser clones of _____ who appeared from her silambu (anklet)
Kartikeya.fact: These nine men were borne by nine lesser clones of Shakti who appeared from her silambu (anklet).

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Shavite puranas such as _____, Shiva Purana and Skanda Purana state that Ganesha is the elder of the two
Kartikeya.fact: Shavite puranas such as Ganesha Purana, Shiva Purana and Skanda Purana state that Ganesha is the elder of the two.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: 'Army of Devas'; as her husband was '_____' lit
Kartikeya.fact: 'Army of Devas'; as her husband was 'Devasenapati' lit.

Kartikeya.question: 'Commander of army of _____')
Kartikeya.fact: In Sanskrit literature, Kartikeya is married to Devasena (lit. 'Army of Devas'; as her husband was 'Devasenapati' lit.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States

Kartikeya.fact: Devasena is described as the daughter of Daksha in the Mahabharata, while Skanda Purana considers her as the daughter of Indra and his wife Shachi.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: In Tamil literature, he has two consorts: _____ (identified with Devasena) and Valli
Kartikeya.fact: In Tamil literature, he has two consorts: Devayanai (identified with Devasena) and Valli.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: In Tamil folklore, both _____ and Valli were daughters of Vishnu in the previous birth
Kartikeya.fact: In Tamil literature, he has two consorts: Devayanai (identified with Devasena) and Valli. In Tamil folklore, both Devasena and Valli were daughters of Vishnu in the previous birth.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: When they reincarnated, _____ was adopted as the daughter of Indra as a result of her penance and Valli was born on the Earth
Kartikeya.fact: In Tamil folklore, both Devasena and Valli were daughters of Vishnu in the previous birth. When they reincarnated, Devasena was adopted as the daughter of Indra as a result of her penance and Valli was born on the Earth.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: However, both were destined to marry the son of _____
Kartikeya.fact: However, both were destined to marry the son of Shiva.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States

Kartikeya.fact: For example, the term Kumara appears in hymn 5.2 of the Rig Veda. Kartikeya.fact: For example, the term Kumara appears in hymn 5.2 of the Rig Veda. Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: The text contains over 81,000 verses, and is part of _____ literature
Kartikeya.fact: The text contains over 81,000 verses, and is part of Shaivite literature.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: The text has been an important historical record and influence on the Hindu traditions related to war-god _____
Kartikeya.fact: Kartikeya forms the main theme of Skanda Purana, the largest Mahapurana, a genre of eighteen Hindu religious texts. While the text is named after Skanda (Kartikeya), he does not feature either more or less prominently in the text than in other Shiva-related Puranas.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: The earliest text titled _____ likely existed by the sixth century CE, but the Skanda Purana that has survived into the modern era exists in many versions
Kartikeya.fact: The earliest text titled Skanda Purana likely existed by the sixth century CE, but the Skanda Purana that has survived into the modern era exists in many versions.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Korravai is often identified as the mother of _____
Kartikeya.fact: Extant Sangam literature works dated between the third century BCE and the fifth century CE glorify Murugan, "the red god seated on the blue peacock, who is ever young and resplendent," as "the favoured god of the Tamils". Korravai is often identified as the mother of Murugan.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States

Kartikeya.fact: Extant Sangam literature works dated between the third century BCE and the fifth century CE glorify Murugan, "the red god seated on the blue peacock, who is ever young and resplendent," as "the favoured god of the Tamils". Korravai is often identified as the mother of Murugan.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: He is called _____ and described as a god of beauty and youth, with such exaltations as "his body glows like the sun rising from the emerald sea"
Kartikeya.fact: He is called Murugu and described as a god of beauty and youth, with such exaltations as "his body glows like the sun rising from the emerald sea".

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: The ancient Tamil lexicon _____ identifies the name Vel with the slayer of Tarakasura
Kartikeya.fact: The ancient Tamil lexicon Pinkalandai identifies the name Vel with the slayer of Tarakasura.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: The Arya Kanikrodhavajrakumarabodhisattava Sadhanavidhi Sutra (T _____) features a section for the recitation of a mantra dedicated to the deity, where he is also paired with Isvara
Kartikeya.fact: The Arya Kanikrodhavajrakumarabodhisattava Sadhanavidhi Sutra (T 1796) features a section for the recitation of a mantra dedicated to the deity, where he is also paired with Isvara.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: The sixteenth-century _____ text Jinakalamali mentions him as a guardian god
Kartikeya.fact: The sixteenth-century Siamese text Jinakalamali mentions him as a guardian god.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Similarly, sculptures show him with either one or six heads, with the six head iconography dated to post-_____ era
Kartikeya.fact: Similarly, sculptures show him with either one or six heads, with the six head iconography dated to post-Gupta Empire era.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: He wields a divine spear known as the vel, granted to him by _____
Kartikeya.fact: He wields a divine spear called the vel, granted to him by Parvati.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: His vahana or mount is depicted as a peacock, known as _____
Kartikeya.fact: His vahana or mount is depicted as a peacock, called Paravani.

Kartikeya.fact: He was historically the patron deity of the Yaudheyas, as well as the many other ancient northern and western Hindu kingdoms. Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: Mahasena was also featured by the _____ following their contact with the Yaudheyas, who then incorporated Mahasena's religious and militant iconography on their coins through syncretism
Kartikeya.fact: Mahasena was also featured by the Kushan Empire following their contact with the Yaudheyas, who then incorporated Mahasena's religious and militant iconography on their coins through syncretism.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: After the seventh century, _____'s importance diminished while his brother Ganesha's importance rose in the west and north, while in the south the legends of Murugan continued to grow
Kartikeya.fact: Later Guptas Emperors, specifically Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta, were patrons of Kartikeya as mentioned in the Bilsad pillar inscription which mentions a temple dedicated to Mahasena. After the seventh century, Skanda's importance diminished while his brother Ganesha's importance rose in the west and north, while in the south the legends of Murugan continued to grow.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States

Kartikeya.fact: According to Raman Varadara, Murugan, originally regarded as a Tamil deity, underwent a process of adoption and incorporation into the pantheon of North Indian deities.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States

Kartikeya.fact: He is considered a uniter, championing the attributes of both Shaivism and Vaishnavism (which revere Shiva and Vishnu as their supreme deities, respectively).

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: According to _____, as Murugan, he embodies the "cultural and religious whole that comprises South Indian Shaivism"
Kartikeya.fact: According to Fred Clothey, as Murugan, he embodies the "cultural and religious whole that comprises South Indian Shaivism".

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States
Kartikeya.question: He is a central philosopher and a key exponent of _____ theology, as well as the patron deity of the Tamil language
Kartikeya.fact: Kartikeya's theology is most developed in the Tamil texts and in the Shaiva Siddhanta tradition. He is a central philosopher and a key exponent of Shaiva Siddhanta theology, as well as the patron deity of the Tamil language.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States

Kartikeya.fact: According to Fred Clothey, as Murugan, he embodies the "cultural and religious whole that comprises South Indian Shaivism". Originally, Murugan was not worshipped as a god, but rather as an exalted ancestor, heroic warrior and accomplished Siddhar born in the Kurinji landscape.

Kartikeya.subject: Indian States

Kartikeya.fact: Skanda was regarded as a philosopher in his role as Subramanhya, while Murugan was similarly regarded as the teacher of Tamil literature and poetry.

Kartikeya.fact: Despite the changes, his portrayal was multi-faceted, with significant differences between Skanda and Murugan until the late Vijayanagara Empire, when he was accepted as a single deity with diverse facets.

Kartikeya.fact: In Chinese Buddhism, Skanda (also sometimes called Kumāra) is called Weituo, a young heavenly general, the guardian deity of local monasteries and the protector of Buddhist dhamma. Ladakh.question: It extends from the _____ in the Karakoram range to the north to the main Great Himalayas to the south
Ladakh.fact: Ladakh (English: /ləˈdɑːk/, Hindustani [ləd̪ːaːx]) is a region administered by India as a union territory and constitutes an eastern portion of the larger Kashmir region that has been the subject of a dispute between India and Pakistan since 1947 and India and China since 1959.  Ladakh is bordered by the Tibet Autonomous Region of China to the east, the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh to the south, both the Indian-administered union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan to the west, and the southwest corner of Xinjiang across the Karakoram Pass in the far north.  It extends from the Siachen Glacier in the Karakoram range to the north to the main Great Himalayas to the south.  The eastern end, consisting of the uninhabited Aksai Chin plains, is claimed by the Indian Government as part of Ladakh, but has been under Chinese control since 1962.  In the past, Ladakh gained importance from its strategic location at the crossroads of important trade routes, but as Chinese authorities closed the borders between Tibet Autonomous Region and Ladakh in the 1960s, international trade dwindled.  Since 1974, the Government of India has encouraged tourism i

Ladakh.fact: The Leh district contains the Indus, Shyok and Nubra river valleys.  The Kargil district contains the Suru, Dras and Zanskar river valleys.  The main populated regions are these river valleys, but the mountain slopes also support pastoral Changpa nomads.  The main religious groups in the region are Muslims (46%, mainly Shia), Buddhists (40%, mainly Tibetan Buddhists), and Hindus (12%) with the remaining 2% made of other religions.  Ladakh is both the largest and the second least populous union territory of India.  Its culture and history are closely related to those of Tibet.  As Ladakh is strategically important, the Indian military maintains a strong presence in the region

Ladakh.fact: Today, however, it commonly refers only to Maryul, which is administered by India, while the term Baltistan is now used for Baltiyul, which is administered by Pakistan.  Medieval Islamic scholars called Ladakh the "Great Tibet" (derived from Turko-Arabic Ti-bat, meaning "highland"); Baltistan and other trans-Himalayan states in Kashmir's vicinity were referred to as "Little Tibets".  It has also been called Ma-Lo-Pho (by Hiuen Tsang) or Lal Bhumi.  Names in the local language include Kanchapa (Land of snow) and Ripul (Country of mountains).  == History == === Ancient history === Rock carvings found in many parts of Ladakh indicate that the area has been inhabited from Neolithic times.  Ladakh's earliest inhabitants were nomads known as Kampa.  Later settlements were established by Mons from Kullu and Brokpas who originated from Gilgit

Ladakh.fact: Usually, one son from every family was obliged to master the Tibetan script in order to read the holy books.  The Moravian Mission opened a school in Leh in October 1889, and the Wazir-i Wazarat (ex officio Joint Commissioner with a British officer) of Baltistan and Ladakh ordered that every family with more than one child should send one of them to school. The school taught Tibetan, Urdu, English, Geography, Sciences, Nature study, Arithmetic, Geometry and Bible study.  It is still in existence today. Lamassu.fact: Lama, Lamma, or Lamassu (Cuneiform: 𒀭𒆗, an.kal; Sumerian: dlammař; later in Akkadian: lamassu; sometimes called a lamassuse) is a Mesopotamian protective deity. Initially depicted as a goddess in Sumerian times, when it was called Lamma, it was later depicted from Assyrian times as a hybrid of a human, bird, and either a bull or lion—specifically having a human head, the body of a bull or a lion, and bird wings, under the name Lamassu.
